output.summary: The ED length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours), not ED work-up. Nurse hours per visit, grid compliance and vacancies are flat or better, and volume, acuity and bed capacity are unchanged. Boarding jumped in March when hospitalist rounding moved to 09:30 with new admissions first. Medical-ward discharges slid later, while surgical wards did not change. The 4 West huddle pilot used rotation-assigned days and cut boarding from 4.6 to 2.3 hours. So the cause is later medical discharges, not ED understaffing. Extend the huddle. Do not fund travel nurses by deferring case managers, and do not pause the huddle. The evening cleaning cut and the triage-provider removal are unquantified rivals.
